sentences.text: Nanocetorhinus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the subclass Neoselachii within the class Chondrichthyes.
Its largest teeth measured no more than 1 millimeter in length.
The genus name combines "nano," meaning dwarfish, and "Cetorhinus," the basking shark, referencing the small resemblance of its teeth to those of the basking shark.
The teeth were simple and irregular with no wear on the cutting edges, suggesting they played a minimal role in grabbing or puncturing meat.
The species N. tuberculatus was described in 2013 by Underwood and Schlogl based on 28 fossilized teeth found in Slovakia.
A second species, N. zeitlingeri, was named in 2020 based on three complete fossilized teeth found in Austria.
Researchers theorized that Nanocetorhinus was a planktivorous shark, though this is not supported by evidence of close relation to the basking shark.
Nanocetorhinus lived between 23.04 and 13.82 million years ago, from the Aquitanian to the Langhian stages.
